summary.intent: Use the GSD manager to run discuss sessions for phases 42 (API unpin integrity), 43 (FUSE write durability), and 44 (IPNS conflict handling), then plan phase 42.
summary.outcome: Completed discuss sessions and committed CONTEXT.md/DISCUSSION-LOG.md for all three phases; completed planning for phase 42 including research, validation strategy, and pattern mapping; created .prettierignore to protect .planning markdown from prettier corruption.

repo: The POST /ipfs/unpin endpoint is protected only by JwtAuthGuard but never reads req.user — any authenticated user can unpin any CID string, making it a cross-tenant data-destruction surface.

Kubo v0.40 runs with the `server` profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (docker/docker-compose.staging.yml:62-72), advertising provider records for every pinned CID to the public DHT — CIDs are not secret.
Web3Auth signup is open (email/OAuth), so any attacker can obtain a valid JWT and then issue arbitrary unpin requests.
All current unpin callers silently ignore errors: web uses `.catch(logger.warn)`, FUSE uses `let _ =` — so a 403 response would surface as a warning log spike, not a user-visible failure.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without unpinning (shared-write.ts:450), so cross-user legitimate unpin via that path doesn't exist.
The upload-compensation path (ipfs.controller.ts:122) fires a global pin/rm on a CID that content-addressed dedup may share with another user.

Concurrent unpin of a deduped CID by two users can race past the refcount check and strand an orphaned Kubo pin — requires a per-CID advisory lock (Postgres xact lock on hash(cid)), not a reconciliation job.
BYO-IPFS capability injects a provider.unpin function but it is not yet wired into the delete flow — only the managed-Kubo path executes unpin today.
A .prettierignore was needed because prettier was mangling regex pipes in .planning markdown tables into table-column syntax.

code.finding: Kubo service config: server profile + swarm port 4001 tcp/udp exposed publicly. Server profile only suppresses local-network discovery; full public DHT participation (and CID advertisement) is retained.
Upload-compensation path issues a global pin/rm using a bare CID with no ownership check — can destroy another user's pin if the CID is content-addressed-deduped.
Writable-share save drops prunedCids from the manifest without calling unpin — intentional, but means revoked share recipients retain the pin.

workflow: On Claude Code, GSD plan/execute must run inline (not as background agents) because a backgrounded agent lacks the Agent/Task tool needed to spawn the plan-checker and worktree-isolated executors.
The discuss workflow produces three artifacts per phase: CONTEXT.md (decisions for downstream agents), DISCUSSION-LOG.md (rationale trail), and DISCUSS-CHECKPOINT.json (structured decision record).
Presenting a question menu in response to a direct factual question is an anti-pattern — users expect a direct answer followed optionally by options, not options in place of the answer.

A read-only pin-ls drift report (detect orphaned Kubo pins not in pinned_cids ∪ pending_unpins) is safer than auto-GC: it gives visibility without risk of destroying pins the relay path didn't create.

friction: Phase 44 commits silently failed on the first attempt — git log still showed phase 43 as HEAD; required a visible retry with output to diagnose and re-commit.
STATE.md was omitted from the initial phase 44 commit and needed a separate follow-up commit.

The assistant answered the 'downside of a loud 403' question by presenting another AskUserQuestion menu instead of directly answering, requiring the user to explicitly call out the non-answer before getting a plain response.
open_items: Wire provider.unpin into BYO-IPFS delete flows — deferred out of phase 42 scope, which targets only the managed-Kubo path.
Read-only pin-ls drift report to surface pre-existing orphaned pins (historical compensation failures, ops pins predating quota tracking) — detection only, no auto-GC.
Phases 43 (FUSE write durability) and 44 (IPNS conflict handling) are discussed but not yet planned — planning sessions still to run.
Per-CID Postgres advisory lock (hash(cid)) around the delete+refcount decision to close the concurrent-unpin dedup race — must be implemented to make the outbox airtight.
